narrative:
The model estimated a 39% chance that you would be a bad credit risk. That does not mean default is certain, but it was above the bank’s approval cutoff, so your loan was denied.

The most important factor was your checking account status. Since having no checking account is common among approved applicants, this actually leaned toward good credit. The next strongest factor was the loan purpose: a new car. New-car requests are much less common among approved borrowers, so this pushed the decision toward bad credit. The third factor was having a co-applicant. Very few approved applicants had a co-applicant, so this also increased the perceived risk. Your shorter 10-month term and smaller 1,287 DM request compared with approved averages were more favorable, but they did not outweigh those concerns.

To improve future chances, ask the bank which specific factors most affected the denial. Consider providing stronger savings or banking documentation, reducing or restructuring the request, and discussing whether the co-applicant is necessary. Reapplying after addressing these points may lead to a better outcome.
